draft.title: Time dilation and length contraction
card: the time between two events measured in a frame where both events happen at the same place. A clock moving with the events measures it.
the length of an object measured in the frame where the object is at rest.
An observer moving relative to these measures a longer time and a shorter length. The time is t = γt₀ and the length is L = L₀/γ, where γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) and γ is always 1 or more.
The length shortens only along the direction of motion. The effects are tiny at everyday speeds and large close to the speed of light.
draft.remember: Own frame gives the shortest time and the longest length. Moving observers see time stretched and length shrunk.

a.q: A rocket passes Earth at 0.8c. Which measurement is a proper time?
opts: A rocket clock timing two events on the rocket
An Earth clock timing two events on the rocket
An Earth clock timing two events on Earth, viewed from the rocket
A rocket clock timing two events on Earth
a.why: Proper time is measured by one clock present at both events, so the rocket clock timing rocket events gives it. The Earth clock timing rocket events sees them at different places, so it is not proper time.
a.clue: Which clock is at the same place as both events?

b.q: A spacecraft is 120 m long when at rest. It passes a station at 0.6c, where γ = 1.25. What length does the station crew measure, and what do the spacecraft crew measure?
opts: 96 m by the station crew, 120 m by the spacecraft crew
120 m by the station crew, 96 m by the spacecraft crew
150 m by the station crew, 120 m by the spacecraft crew
96 m by the station crew, 96 m by the spacecraft crew
b.why: The 120 m is the proper length, measured by the spacecraft crew in the frame where it is at rest. The station crew see it moving, so L = 120 ÷ 1.25 = 96 m. Multiplying by γ gives 150 m, but moving observers measure a shorter length, not a longer one.
b.clue: Whose frame is the spacecraft at rest in?

proposal.remember: Own frame gives the shortest time and the longest length. Moving observers see time stretched and length shrunk.

a.q: A rocket passes Earth at 0.8c. Which measurement is a proper time?
opts: A rocket clock timing two events at one spot on the rocket
An Earth clock timing two events at one spot on the rocket
A rocket clock timing two events at one spot on Earth
Two Earth clocks timing the rocket between two planets
a.why: The rocket clock sits at that spot on the rocket, so it is present at both events and measures proper time. An Earth clock sees that spot move, so the two events happen at different places in its frame. In the same way, a spot on Earth moves past the rocket, and two separate clocks mean the events are at different places.
a.clue: In which frame do both events happen at the same place?
